title: This Is It: 2027 Porsche Boxster EV, Spied Camo-Free
summary: Porsche stopped taking orders for the 982-generation 718 Boxster and 718 Cayman in September 2025, 14 months after announcing that both gas-powered models would be replaced by EVs. body_markdown:
Porsche stopped taking orders for the 982-generation[718 Boxster](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/last-drive-the-718-boxster-gts-4-0-will-be-hard-to-beat/) and 718 Cayman[in September 2025](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/as-expected-porsche-halts-new-orders-of-ice-powered-boxster-and-cayman/) , 14 months after[announcing](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-confirms-the-end-of-gas-powered-boxster-cayman/) that both gas-powered models would be replaced by EVs. Those plans reportedly changed as demand for electric cars dropped: In December 2025, rumors[claimed](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/report-porsche-pulls-another-u-turn-as-next-cayman-and-boxster-to-get-gas-engines/) that internal-combustion models would be part of the range after all, and in early 2026, reports suggested the EVs[had been canceled](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-718-ev-canceled-report/) . Now, there’s another twist. While nothing is official, recent spy shots showing the 2027 Porsche Boxster EV camo-free indicate that it’s headed to production.


Taken on a track, the pictures of a German-registered test mule leave little to the imagination. The next Boxster’s front end borrows styling cues such as rectangular lights from Porsche’s current crop of EVs, including[the Macan](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2026-porsche-macan-gts-specs-suspension-pictures/) and[the Taycan](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-expands-second-generation-taycan-model-lineup/) . The look is both retro and futuristic. On one hand, it reminds us of the slant-nose 911s built by the factory and by the aftermarket during the 1980s. On the other hand, the new Boxster looks a lot like[the 2021 Mission R concept](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-mission-r-is-a-1100-hp-race-car-for-customer-teams/) when you see it from the front.


Out back, thin rear lights create another visual link between the next Boxster and Porsche’s other EVs. Together with the fake “intakes” on the rear haunches, which appear to be stickers, the lack of exhaust cut-outs in the diffuser all but confirm that we’re looking at an electric car. The proportions remain remarkably Boxster-like in spite of the drivetrain change, however.

There’s no word yet on the car’s battery-electric driveline, but we expect Porsche to do its best to dial in the kind of handling enthusiasts expect from a sports car with a mid-mounted engine. Handling has always been a big part of the Boxster’s appeal, after all. Rear-wheel-drive will undoubtedly come standard, and dual-motor all-wheel-drive might be available on some of the higher-powered variants. If so, it would be the first time that Porsche offers a Boxster with four driven wheels.


Keep in mind that the gasoline-powered Boxster hasn’t necessarily reached the end of its road. Though Porsche is currently testing the EV, which it has been developing for years, and the roadster seems likely to debut with battery power, there’s still a strong demand for gasoline-burning sports cars. In addition, unverified rumors claim the platform is being re-engineered for ICE power. Retrofitting an EV platform with an engine is more difficult than it sounds, but that doesn’t mean Porsche won’t do so sooner or later.


We still have a lot to learn about the 2027 Boxster EV. Porsche hasn’t announced when we’ll see the model, but this camo-free test mule hints that an official unveiling is imminent. When it lands, the next Boxster will be the only electric sports car in the Volkswagen Group’s portfolio. It won’t stand alone for very long: Audi[is planning to use](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/electric-audi-concept-c-confirmed-tt/) Porsche’s PPE Sport platform to underpin the hotly anticipated follow-up to[the TT](http://hagerty.com/media/news/audi-tt-roadster-final-edition-is-a-gorgeous-green-going-away-present/) . The coupe was previewed by[the Concept C](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/audi-steers-new-course-with-concept-c/) unveiled in September 2025.
